title: A Drift-Aware Reliability Assessment Framework for Evaluating Predictive Maintenance Models Under Evolving Operational Conditions
content: Predictive maintenance (PdM) models are increasingly developed to predict equipment failures and reduce unplanned downtime, yet their long-term reliability degrades as the distribution of sensor data shifts under operational conditions, a phenomenon known as concept drift. Despite growing embrace, no existing framework systematically quantifies this Degradation or supports evidence-based retraining decisions in deployed PdM systems to address this need. We introduced the Drift-Aware Reliability Assessment Framework (DARAF), which assessed model accuracy, reliability, and predictability by examining specific types of changes in operational data over the course of a PdM system's active life. The framework consists of four mutually supporting components: DSI, PDR, DRI, and RLM. Overall, the findings showed an average degradation of 10.68% to 18.37%, with little to no benefit from adaptive (dynamic) strategies for improving the reliability of a PdM system. This study highlights a basis for future training model decision-making processes of PdM systems.
